prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its active forms that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full round-1 exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part, B046, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. All six of us arrived at it independently, and that is not the argument. The argument is that each credited contribution is a discovery in the strict sense. Holst established the secretion and the active forms of GLP-1, Mojsov identified and synthesised the active peptide, and Drucker connected proglucagon-derived peptide biology to receptor mechanism and to the first therapeutic proof of concept. The result is a fully mature chain, independently confirmed for decades and now supported by large outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal disease. No other shortlisted achievement combines that originality, durability and documented patient benefit with an attribution that can be defended in three names. A second part would force a reduction of this trio, and I see no candidate whose case is strong enough to justify weakening B046 to make room for it.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and the round-1 exchange did not remove it. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener's group is contested, Habener is not among the credited names, and I cannot settle that record from the supplied evidence. Excluding Knudsen means the citation honours physiology and not the engineering of long-acting analogues that put the drugs in patients, and a reader could say the prize ignores the step that made the discovery a medicine. I accept that a three-name cut from four credited people is a judgement, not a finding. I still think it is the more defensible reading of what the prize rewards, but I hold it as a judgement.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would consider replacing Mojsov with Knudsen if Mojsov's priority is not sound, and asks whether the citation should acknowledge drug development explicitly.
responses.response: I considered the swap seriously and decline it. Mojsov's contribution, identifying and synthesising GLP-1(7-36) as the active form, is a discovery-level step that the later analogue work depended on. Knudsen's work, however important to patients, is the optimisation of a known peptide for pharmacokinetics. The contested priority against Habener is a reason for care in the wording and not for exchanging her for someone from a different category of contribution. I would keep the citation on the physiology and its enabling of therapies. The words 'enabled incretin-based therapies' acknowledge the clinical outcome without claiming that drug design is itself the credited discovery. I would record in the deliberations that Knudsen's development work is central to the medicines, so that the omission is stated openly.

responses.point: Linnarsson keeps Mojsov but names Holst and Drucker alone as a thinner but defensible fallback, and asks whether a second part such as B040 would improve the configuration or only dilute a strong single-achievement prize.
responses.response: I agree that a second part would dilute the prize here, and for a specific reason, which is the three-person cap. Adding June and Sadelain would leave one or at most two GLP-1 names, which would break the physiological arc, and I would not choose that trade. I also disagree mildly with the Holst and Drucker fallback. It is defensible, but it leaves out the identification of the active peptide, which is the link between proglucagon processing and the pharmacology. If Mojsov's priority proved untenable from the record, I would prefer to say so and reconsider the trio than to drop her silently. On the supplied evidence I do not think that point is reached, so I keep her.

responses.point: Sandberg describes the long-acting analogue work as industrial optimisation, and supports a narrow June and Sadelain pairing if B040 is considered, with B031 as an alternative.
responses.response: I share the view that the analogue work is optimisation and not discovery, and I would use it as the reason for the physiology-only reading. I am less sure about calling it merely industrial, since the engineering of half-life and receptor selectivity needed real scientific insight. That is why I treat the Knudsen omission as a real cost and not a technicality. On B040 I stay with June and Sadelain as the cleaner pair. I keep B040 above B031 as an alternative because its patient benefit is established, whereas the clinical consequences of the unfolded protein response remain prospective. Sandberg's choice of B031 is a reasonable alternative and I would not object to it in a later year.

responses.point: Perlmann favours Hall with Schreiber for TOR, and prefers to keep the prize on the physiology of GLP-1 without folding in drug development.
responses.response: I agree with the second point and stay with my earlier disagreement on the first. The TOR discovery is a genetic one, and the mammalian nutrient-sensing work that gives it physiological meaning is closer to Sabatini than to the chemistry of rapamycin binding. I do not see TOR as a competitor to B046 this year, because the clinical reach beyond transplant and oncology is not yet shown, and so the Hall, Sabatini or Schreiber question does not need to be settled now. My 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann concerns dopamine neurons and does not bear on B046 or B015.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active peptide holds against Habener's group cannot be settled from the supplied record. I would revisit the trio only if the committee finds that the record clearly undermines her credit.
Whether the committee will accept the exclusion of Knudsen. I consider it a judgement on what counts as discovery, and a reasonable member could differ.

If the committee prefers two parts, I have not identified a partner for B046 that justifies reducing the GLP-1 trio. B040 with June and Sadelain would be the best candidate, but Eshhar's original chimeric receptor remains an unresolved gap.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with B046, my preferred part. My profile records a 2009 co-authored paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons, which does not concern any shortlisted discovery. My locomotor circuit work makes me a user of optogenetic tools (B049), with no documented connection to its credited names, which is why I have been careful not to let that familiarity raise B049 above an alternative. I see no recusal need on the provided record, and nothing in round 1 changes this.
